etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French presentation (French présentation), from Latin praesentātiōnem, accusative singular of praesentātiō (“representation, exhibition”). Morphologically present +‎ -ation

definitions.definition: The act of presenting, or something presented.

quote.citation: 1594–1597, Richard Hooker, edited by J[ohn] S[penser], Of the Lawes of Ecclesiastical Politie, […], London:  […]  Will[iam] Stansby [for Matthew Lownes], published 1611, →OCLC, (please specify the page):
quote.text: Prayers are sometimes a presentation of mere desires.

definitions.definition: An award given to someone on a special occasion.
Money given as a wedding gift.
A lecture or speech given in front of an audience.
A slideshow created on a computer.
(medicine) The symptoms and other possible indications of disease, trauma, etc., that are exhibited by a patient who has sought, or has otherwise come to, the attention of a physician.
(medicine) The position of the foetus in the uterus at birth.
(fencing) Offering one's blade for engagement by the opponent.
(mathematics) The specification of a group by generators and relators.
The act or right of offering a clergyman to the bishop or ordinary for institution in a benefice.

quote.citation: 1765–1769, William Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, (please specify |book=I to IV), Oxford, Oxfordshire:  […]  Clarendon Press, →OCLC:
quote.text: If the bishop admits the patron's presentation, the clerk so admitted is next to be instituted by him.

definitions.definition: (immunology) The preparation of antigen fragments during the immune response.
